title: The French Opera House: orchestra, prices and fate
summary: The pit held about 50 men, the gallery cost 35 cents, and the building burned in 1919.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: You read my history. I'm wondering, since you remember the old French opera, I know it's hard to think back that many years, too, when you were a boy and went to the French opera, but can you remember anything about the orchestra, how many players, is it a pretty big...

You mean in the orchestra, at the opera? In the pit, yes. Oh my gosh, yes. I don't think, far as I can remember, there were under 50 men in the pit. Regular symphonic outfit. Regular symphonic outfit. Oh yes, yes. It was a monster thing.
Did they have opera about every night? Yes.
Uh-huh. You'd go only to five. And the thing that made it nice for us, that you could go in the gallery for 35 cents. 35? Mm-hmm.
Yeah, and we heard some very fine, some very fine artists.
Can you remember any famous singers or rich opera?
Of course, I don't know if they would match up with the present day opera singers, but in those days, we thought they were very wonderful.
I always heard too, the New Orleans French Opera was one of the best in the country.
I don't think they have that anymore.
Oh no, they do have some opera at the auditorium now. Maybe...
Yeah, but they're not the original New Orleans opera company. Oh no, that opera house... They don't have their own opera company as they did in those days.
They don't even have the opera house, it's a municipal auditorium. Oh yeah. The opera house burned down in 1919. Oh.
So, uh... That's the old opera house on Bourbon Street. On Bourbon and Tulips.

Yeah. It's a big parking lot. Yeah. Is that so? It's a big parking lot. All the nightclubs are right, started all around in there, nightclubs, and strip joints, you know, for all the strip girls. That's all.
Sometimes I might run down there and look the field of... I haven't been there in. Oh.
